definitions.explanation: Describes clothing or items that come with an attached hood. Used as a modifier before nouns to specify that the item has a hood.

examples.japanese: フード{付|つ}きのパーカーを{買|か}った。
{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}はフード{付|つ}きのジャケットが{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: On rainy days, a hooded jacket is convenient.

examples.japanese: フード{付|つ}きのコートは{暖|あたた}かいけれど、{自転車|じてんしゃ}に{乗|の}るときはフードが{邪魔|じゃま}になることがある。
examples.english: A hooded coat is warm, but the hood can get in the way when riding a bicycle.

notes:
Composed of フード (hood, from English) + {付|つ}き (attached, with). The suffix {付|つ}き is extremely productive in Japanese and can be attached to many nouns to mean "equipped with" or "including" (e.g., {朝食|ちょうしょく}{付|つ}き — with breakfast, カメラ{付|つ}き — with a camera).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フード{付|つ}きパーカー: hooded parka
- フード{付|つ}きコート: hooded coat
- フード{付|つ}きジャケット: hooded jacket
- フード{付|つ}きタオル: hooded towel

SIMILAR WORDS:
- フードなし: without a hood — the opposite
- {付|つ}き: with, equipped with — the suffix by itself, applicable to many items
